headline: On 23 Jul 2026, shares of the telehealth firms Teladoc Health and Amwell slipped on the day OpenAI let US ChatGPT users link their medical records and health apps to the chatbot.
score_reason: Pool score 6, lowered by 2: the Stocktwits page is dated 23 Jul 2026, almost three months old, and the share moves are one outlet's one-day market note.
importance_line: US ChatGPT users can optionally link their health records so the chatbot answers from their own data, and Teladoc and Amwell shares fell on the day, but this is July news resurfacing and the link between the feature and the share drop is Stocktwits' own reading.
summary: A Stocktwits market report dated 23 Jul 2026 says Teladoc Health (TDOC) shares were down about 3% and American Well (Amwell, AMWL) about 8% when it was written, on the day OpenAI widened the Health section of ChatGPT for US users, letting them optionally link Apple Health, supported US hospital records, One Medical or Function Health so the chatbot can refer to their medications, lab results and visits. OpenAI says linked data gets extra encryption, will not train its models or target ads, and can be unlinked whenever the user chooses, while Stocktwits itself argues the feature overlaps with what telehealth firms sell, which is its reading and not a reported effect.
notes: OLDER NEWS RE-DATED: Google News lists it as 13 Oct 2026, but the Stocktwits page metadata (datePublished and dateModified) is 2026-07-23 and the text says 'Thursday' (13 Oct 2026 is a Tuesday). The feature is confirmed inside the article as OpenAI's own announcement, relayed by one outlet; no second outlet was read, though a HuffPost headline of 3 Oct 2026 about uploading medical records to ChatGPT Health shows the feature was in use by October. Score lowered from 6 to 4 because the event is stale.
